ceiling_directive: Establish the augmented paired tail-rank experiment and a matching honest-set ambiguity frontier on the heterogeneous-tail model class used by the public Leimenstoll–Schienle theorem, with an explicit inclusion or extension covering the collision arrays.
improvement_directive: Add the root-k_n common-index coordinate and joint exceedance-overlap intensity, then prove a uniform paired-process expansion that calibrates a nonconstant honest direction set. Complete the same-class opposite-orientation contiguity lower bound so its ambiguity rate matches that procedure.
critique: The positive results are sequential population collision curves for a finite-threshold contrast over a specially constructed triangular-array class; they provide neither observed-law orientation identification nor a sampling limit, rate, or uniform remainder for the empirical contrast. The experiment theorem only disproves one four-coordinate summed-marginal representation by exhibiting omitted common-index variation and overlap covariance; it does not construct the augmented experiment or establish a general impossibility result. The only proved direction set is the constant full alphabet with ambiguity probability one, while the public [Leimenstoll–Schienle preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.22957) already supplies heterogeneous-tail CTC estimation and inference outside this collision problem. Although the framing explicitly disclaims the missing inferential results, the note supports “frontier” only as population transition and scale geometry, not as a matched ambiguity or inference frontier.
